item.description:

Institution: ROMA "Tor Vergata", Roma, Rm
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-08 Endocrinologia, nefrologia e scienze dell'alimentazione e del benessere

The project aims to investigate the effects of polyphenols derived from extra virgin olive oil, olives, and olive oil industry by-products obtained through circular economy approaches, on the health of professional athletes and patients with metabolic syndrome, using a multidisciplinary approach. Cross-over clinical studies will be conducted on 40 professional athletes and 60 patients with metabolic syndrome, assessing oxidative stress, inflammation, antioxidant capacity, body composition, endothelial function, and physical performance. item.title: Incarico post-doc: Small Non-Coding RNAs in Testicular Tumors and Male Reproductive Health: Identification of Diagnostic Biomarkers and Assessment of Chemotherapy-Induced Effects on the Epigenome (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-06 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-26 Scienze tecn. di medicina di labor., sc. delle prof. sanit. tecn. diagnostiche, assist. e della prevenzione, sc. delle prof. sanit. della riabilitazione, sc. tecn. med. e chirurg. avanzate

Testicular tumors are a heterogeneous group of neoplasms for which currently available biomarkers still show limited accuracy and sensitivity. Some miRNAs have demonstrated significant diagnostic potential in testicular germ cell tumors (TGCTs); however, data on their expression profiles in serum and seminal plasma from patients with seminoma and non-germ cell tumors, such as Leydig cell tumors, are lacking. The first aim of this study is therefore to characterize the profile of small non-coding RNAs (miRNAs and piRNAs) in malignant and benign testicular tumors. item.title: Incarico post-doc: Identification of post-transcriptional modifications of tumor suppressors in tumorigenic processes and their role in modulating the expression of immune checkpoints (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-06 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Medicine / 06/MEDS-02 Patologia generale e patologia clinica

Colorectal carcinoma (CRC) frequently harbors mutations in tumor suppressor genes—including *TP53*—that are associated with tumor progression and treatment resistance. Mutant p53 (mutp53) has been shown to sustain HDAC6 expression, thereby promoting DNA damage repair and resistance to endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress via ATF6. Preliminary data suggest that ATF6 increases TRAPPC4 expression, promoting the trafficking of PD-L1 to the cell membrane. Furthermore, HDAC6 deacetylates MSH2 and promotes its degradation, thereby impairing mismatch repair and contributing to mutation accumulation, neoantigen production, and immune checkpoint expression. The activity will focus on coordinating the research conducted by the university and hospital teams involved in the OUTREACH project, funded by Fondazione Cariplo (Ref. 2024-3450), which assesses the clinical, social and area-level determinants of frailty among older people in Brescia. The project involves an observational study and epidemiological analysis of anonymised data to develop predictive models for health and social care planning.
